# Rear Hatch Rotopax Mounting

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> **Some safety-critical values on this page are not confirmed** (marked [Unverified] or [Partial]): they come from one source or are only partly supported. Verify against the factory service manual before use; later runs re-check them against new sources.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

Extract fasteners from behind the first-aid box and beneath handles to free clips. [t472]

[Partial] Install the rear hatch or gate to support water containers, gas cans, and a ladder. [t472]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. [Partial] Extract two 7mm fasteners from behind the first-aid box and a pair of 10mm nuts beneath the handles before tugging lightly to free the clips.
2. Mark drilling locations with masking tape and a marker while aiming for center alignment or adjusting if keeping an Xterra badge is desired.
3. [Partial] Use a level to verify that both the bumper and floor are level before ensuring the mount aligns similarly.
4. Double-check all measurements, then drill a small pilot hole followed by 1/4" holes matching the stock hardware size.
5. Remove the masking tape and any burs from the drilled area, then apply paint to the bare metal for rust protection.
6. Use cardboard or similar material to determine the largest cut possible for the sheet metal and trace where tabs must be removed so it sits flat against existing metal.
7. Press against the rear panel's contour to align it, then scribe four spots for drilling.
8. Drill out the marked holes in the sheet metal.
9. Thread bolts and washers through the four holes of the mounting plate, then slide on bonding washers to prevent bolt movement.
10. Insert the four bolts through the holes in the hatch, apply RTV sealant to the hatch for grip, and optionally add some to the inside of the bolt threads as well.
11. Place the sheet metal into position and secure it with washers and nuts while ensuring nothing buckles under pressure.
12. Use cardboard or paper to measure how long steel bars can be cut so they remain vertical when the hatch is closed, marking this length based on proximity to supports and curve placement.
13. Cut the steel bars to the measured length and drill them out accordingly.
14. Measure for horizontal aluminum tubing that bridges the steel bars to add rigidity, ensuring one side fits a 1/4" hole and the other accommodates a socket head.
15. Assemble all components except rubber shims as per diagram instructions, tightening in a criss-cross pattern slowly while watching for buckling.
16. Insert rubber shims between the steel bar ends and the hatch to remove any leftover slack once all fasteners are snug.
17. Insert 1/8" thick pieces about 3" square that extend past the steel, then wedge in 1/16" thick pieces tightly between the hatch and steel bar for all four edges.
18. Clean up sharp edges with duct tape to prevent vibration and ensure rubber shims stay in place without relocating.
19. Reassemble everything onto the vehicle and perform a final check by yanking on the extended part of the Rotopax mount while the hatch is closed.

_Procedure reported by [t472]. Photos of this job are in the source: <https://www.xterranation.org/index.php?threads/how-to-rotopax-rear-hatch-rear-gate-install.10105/>_

## Specifications

- **Strut load capacity**: 175# to 200# [t472] ([Partial] [Unverified] single report)

## Tips & gotchas

- Orient the mounting plate so the longer distance between bolts is horizontal to better handle vertical curve. [t472]
- [Partial] Use cardboard templates for both cutting sheet metal tabs and determining steel bar lengths. [t472]
- [Partial] Use galvanized bonded sealing washers with rubber attached to prevent metal-on-paint rubbing. [t472]
- Consider using a silver vinyl badge instead of the standard one for better placement. [t472]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Using closed cell foam or thick rubber directly on flimsy sheet metal, causing it to collapse before compression occurs. [t472]
- Using 200# struts which may buckle under heavy load and cause upper support bracket failure. [t472]
- [Partial] Failing to account for weight distribution when adding extra items like a ladder. [t472]
